test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 30 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Suppose a satellite is 10² km above the ground and it is used to take high resolution images of objects. If a concave mirror is used to form a primary image of an object of size 1.0 m and if the image size is 5 μm and it is inverted, then the principal focus of the concave mirror should be:
solution:
The correct answer is __**-0.5 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Given:**

 
 
• Object size, O = 1.0 m
 
• Image size, I = -5 μm (negative sign indicates an inverted image)
 
• Distance of the object from the mirror, u = -100,000 m (negative since object distance is measured opposite to the direction of the incident light)
 
 
 
• **Formulae Used:**
 
 
• Mirror Equation: (1)/(f)=(1)/(u)+(1)/(v)
 
• Magnification Equation: m=(I)/(O)=(v)/(u)
 
 
 
• **Calculation:**
 
 
• Magnification, m: m=(I)/(O)=frac{-5times 10⁻⁶m}{1.0m}=-5×10⁻⁶
 
• Using the Magnification Equation to Find v (Image Distance): m=(v)/(u) Rightarrow v=mtimes u= -5times 10⁻⁶times -100,000m=0.5m (Image distance v is positive, indicating that the image is real and formed on the opposite side of the mirror).
 
• Using the Mirror Equation to Find f (Focal Length): (1)/(f)=(1)/(u)+(1)/(v)=(1)/(-100,000m)+(1)/(0.5m)=-0.00001+2(1)/(f)=1.99999Rightarrow f=(1)/(1.99999) approx -0.5m (Focal length f is negative, consistent with the nature of concave mirrors).
 
 
 
• **Conclusion:**
 
 
• The focal length of the concave mirror should be -0.5 meters. This focal length ensures the formation of a real, inverted, and highly diminished image as described.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **Sign Convention for Concave Mirror:**

 
• **Object Distance (u):**

 
 
• **Negative **when the object is placed in front of the mirror (real object).
 
• This is because the object is always placed on the left side of the mirror, and the light from the object travels towards the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Image Distance (v):**
 
 
• **Positive **when the image is formed in front of the mirror (real image).
 
• **Negative **when the image is formed behind the mirror (virtual image).
 
• Real images in a concave mirror are formed when the object is placed outside the focal length, and these images appear on the same side as the object but inverted.
 
 
 
• **Focal Length (f):**
 
 
• **Negative **for a concave mirror.
 
• The focal point of a concave mirror is real and is located in front of the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Magnification (m):**
 
 
• **Positive **if the image is upright (**virtual and magnified**).
 
• **Negative **if the image is inverted (**real and may be diminished or magnified**).
 
• Magnification is also considered negative if the image is real because it appears inverted relative to the object.
